# Shared-bath local signs do not by themselves yield local stochastic faults

Status: new analytic obstruction, not independently reviewed. This challenges a proposed many-operation consequence; it does not change any accepted global logical-channel theorem. No novelty claim or lower bound against all randomized compilation is intended.

## Binding distinction from the accepted global-sign theorem

A single GLOBAL sign reverses all K terms together. Every branch then has the SAME quadratic effective dissipator, so the accepted global-sign theorem compares the two branches to one fixed target. Independent LOCAL signs generally change the off-diagonal entries of the leading Gram matrix branch by branch. Their average generator may have diagonal Gram matrix, but the average finite-time channel does not follow from that average generator. This note corrects that proposed local-sign inference; it does not contradict the accepted global-sign theorem or its reset-free epoch composition.

## 1. Exact bounded, rapidly mixing source

Take one stationary classical telegraph source eta(t) in {+1,-1}, flipping at rate lambda. It has mixing time of order 1/lambda. Couple n system qubits through

    H(t)=sqrt(gamma lambda) eta(t) sum_{i=1}^n xi_i Z_i,

where the xi_i are fresh independent fair private signs chosen once at the start of a fixed epoch of duration t>0. Set H0=0. Each local coupling has fixed diffusion strength gamma>0. Define the common integrated phase

    W=sqrt(gamma lambda) integral_0^t eta(s) ds.

Conditional on W and the signs, the system unitary is tensor_i exp(-i xi_i W Z_i). Averaging the signs, independently for each site, gives EXACTLY

    tensor_i [(1-p(W)) Id_i + p(W) Ad_Zi],  p(W)=sin^2 W.

Averaging W therefore yields a Pauli channel, but its Pauli fault probabilities are correlated by the common latent W. For any specified k sites S, the probability that every site in S has a Z fault, irrespective of faults elsewhere, is

    Prob(S subset fault set)=E[sin^(2k) W].

This is an operationally identifiable Pauli-channel coefficient, for example by a system-reference Bell experiment. It is not an arbitrary choice of unraveling.

# One decaying source can still produce arbitrarily high-weight logical faults

Status: root exact counterexample, awaiting independent check. This limits a proposed multi-site extension, not the received global logical-channel theorems.

Take one source qubit with dark state |0>, jump L=sqrt(2)|0><1|, H=|1><1|, and physical generator lambda D[L]. Thus g=h=1, G^dagger H=-2H, kappa=2. Start the source in |1>. Couple n system qubits by

    sqrt(lambda) K_xi,
    K_xi=H tensor sum_(i=1)^n xi_i Z_i,

where each xi_i is an independent private fair sign held for the whole interval. There is no system Hamiltonian. Each local coupling term has norm1 and commutes with H, so it injects no source energy. The source makes at most ONE physical jump. Its first-jump time is Exp(2lambda), independent of the system. The pure-dark effective logical generator is zero since K_xi(|0> tensor I)=0.

Choose positive time T=pi/(2sqrt(lambda)). On the event of no source jump by T, with probability

    q=exp(-2lambda T)=exp(-pi sqrt(lambda)),

every system qubit undergoes exp(-i xi_i pi Z_i/2), which is Z_i up to a global phase. The product channel on this event is exactly conjugation by Z_1...Z_n, regardless of the private signs.

For earlier jump times t, averaging the independent signs turns each local rotation into a dephasing channel with Z-error probability sin^2(sqrt(lambda)t); conditioned on that t, the joint channel is their product. Thus the full averaged channel is a Pauli channel whose all-n-Z error probability is at least q. This statement refers to a genuine Pauli error distribution, not merely a large trace-distance bound or a chosen decomposition with negative weights.

A local-stochastic fault guarantee with size-independent parameter p<1 would require the probability of errors on all n specified sites to be <=p^n. For any fixed lambda, q>0, so choosing n>log(q)/log(p) contradicts that guarantee. Each individual source energy estimate and the expected jump count remain excellent. The shared dwell-time event causes the high-weight tail.

Consequences:

* Small expected energy or jump count alone does not supply a size-independent local fault theorem.
* Independent private signs on local couplings do not remove this common rare-event mechanism.
* The counterexample has unbounded source-to-system fanout. It does NOT rule out bounded-degree geometrically local sources w

## Stationary telegraph example

Conditional on the common integrated phase W, independent private per-site signs average each local unitary into the dephasing mixture with probability sin^2 W. The full averaged channel is therefore a positive mixture of product Pauli channels, and a specified k-site inclusion probability is exactly E sin^{2k} W. This is a channel-identifiable Pauli coefficient, not an arbitrary jump unraveling.

For exactly one rate-lambda telegraph flip, the unnormalized flip-time density is lambda exp(−lambda t) on (0,t). Including both stationary initial signs and the change of variables W=+/−sqrt(gamma lambda)(2u−t) gives precisely lambda exp(−lambda t)/(2sqrt(gamma lambda)) on the stated phase interval. No missing factor of two occurs.
